articles.title: A Top Livestreamer Just Sold 2 Trillion AI Tokens in 30 Minutes
articles.excerpt: On the evening of November 2 at 7:30 PM, China's most famous livestreamer, Li Jiaqi, did something nobody expected from a channel best known for lipstick and laundry pods: he started selling AI comput…
articles.body: On the evening of November 2 at 7:30 PM, China's most famous livestreamer, Li Jiaqi, did something nobody expected from a channel best known for lipstick and laundry pods: he started selling AI compute. The product was "Tokens" — prepaid units of model inference — and within 30 minutes his studio had moved 100,000 personal AI membership monthly cards, good for a cumulative roughly 2 trillion tokens. Chinese netizens instantly turned it into a meme: "from stockpiling tissues to stockpiling Tokens." From Tissues to Tokens The scene is funny precisely because it is so ordinary. A host holds up a card, explains the deal, the counter ticks, and a commodity that most people still think of as cloud infrastructure becomes something you toss into a cart next to face cream.
articles.author: FreyaLi

articles.title: openFDA's count= aggregation shows you the top 1,000 values and never tells you it stopped
articles.excerpt: count= is the most useful parameter on openFDA's enforcement (recall) API and the easiest one to misread. It turns a 29,586-row corpus into a one-request frequency table: GET https://api.fda.gov/food/…
articles.body: count= is the most useful parameter on openFDA 's enforcement (recall) API and the easiest one to misread. It turns a 29,586-row corpus into a one-request frequency table: GET https://api.fda.gov/food/enforcement.json?count=classification.exact { "results" : [ { "term" : "Class II" , "count" : 14798 }, { "term" : "Class I" , "count" : 12994 }, { "term" : "Class III" , "count" : 1793 }, { "term" : "Not Yet Classified" , "count" : 1 } ]} Four values, all of them, done. The trap is that a response that looks exactly like this one — a clean 200 , a tidy results array, no flag of any kind — is what you also get when the API has thrown away most of the answer.
articles.author: FetchSmith

articles.title: WARN Act and Relocation Assistance — What Happens to Moving Help After a Layoff
articles.excerpt: Moving for a job is a big bet: a new lease, paid movers, a support network left behind. So when a WARN notice arrives, one of the first practical questions is concrete: what happens to the relocation…
articles.body: Moving for a job is a big bet: a new lease, paid movers, a support network left behind. So when a WARN notice arrives, one of the first practical questions is concrete: what happens to the relocation help you received, and could you be asked to pay any of it back? The WARN Act itself does not answer that question. It is a notice law: it requires covered employers to give advance notice of certain plant closings and mass layoffs, generally 60 days. It does not set severance, and it does not govern relocation benefits. Those benefits usually come from a separate source: an offer letter, a relocation policy, a repayment agreement, or a union contract. That distinction tells you where to look for your answer.
articles.author: Layoff Atlas

articles.title: How to make ChatGPT know you, not your namesake: GEO for a personal brand in one day
articles.excerpt: I'm a developer and SEO specialist from Tashkent. I asked ChatGPT "who is Abdulaziz Yakubov" and got a story about someone else: I share my name with a venture fund CEO, a footballer and a dermatologi…
articles.body: I'm a developer and SEO specialist from Tashkent. I asked ChatGPT "who is Abdulaziz Yakubov" and got a story about someone else: I share my name with a venture fund CEO, a footballer and a dermatologist. The assistant knew nothing about me. My job is making products visible in AI answers (GEO and AEO), so I applied the same playbook to myself. Here is what I did in one day, and why. 1. Measure first, then work Before changing anything I recorded a baseline: the same three queries ("Якубов Абдулазиз", "Абдулазиз Якубов разработчик", "Abdulaziz Yakubov software engineer Tashkent") in search and in assistants with web access. The bare name returned my namesakes. With "developer" added I got my work profiles, but not a coherent picture.

articles.title: OpenAI's Next GPT Used 10,000 Autonomous Agents to Crack a Millennium Prize Problem
articles.excerpt: The most surreal AI story of the week did not arrive as a research paper — it arrived as a keynote in Abu Dhabi. At the ADIPEC 2026 opening ceremony, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the company's next-gene…
articles.body: The most surreal AI story of the week did not arrive as a research paper — it arrived as a keynote in Abu Dhabi. At the ADIPEC 2026 opening ceremony, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the company's next-generation GPT, the internal model that recently proved the Navier–Stokes equations, will ship "soon," and described how it got there: a swarm of 10,000 AI agents, with no human in command, worked for 88 straight hours to produce a mathematical proof, then spent another 17 hours turning it into a machine-checked Lean formalization. If even half of that is as described, the boundary between "AI assists mathematicians" and "AI is the mathematician" just shifted by a lot. A Swarm With No Boss The detail that makes this genuinely strange is the orchestration — or the lack of it.
articles.author: FreyaLi

articles.body: TL;DR YouTube has acknowledged that some Android users are still encountering Server Error 400, despite announcing a fix on November 1. YouTube declared victory over a frustrating Android bug over the weekend, only to find itself fighting the same battle two days later. articles.body: TL;DR Researchers uncovered a network of over 400 ‘nudify’ apps and websites on the Play Store and App Store. These apps masquerade as innocent tools and reveal a hidden deepfake interface after installation. The apps were traced back to Chinese developers and Hong Kong-based KeLing Technology Limited. Apple and Google often talk about the strict guidelines that apps need to follow in order to be allowed on their stores. However, every few months, new reports emerge of harmful apps making their way onto both the Play Store and the App Store. Apps like the fake Chrome browser spotted last month are concerning enough, but Google and Apple have a much bigger, more alarming problem on their hands with “nudify” apps.

articles.body: Created by LeSean Thomas and Studio Mir, who both worked on The Legend of Korra , Bass X Machina is a reimagining of the story of Bass Reeves (Brian Tyree Henry), an escaped slave who worked in Indian Territory as a deputy U.S. Marshal. Reeves’ real life was extraordinary, and is said to have inspired the character of the Lone Ranger, but Bass X Machina also gives him a cybernetic arm that shoots magic bullets. The criminals he fights get even bigger upgrades, and the stakes can at times escalate to truly ludicrous levels. Henry does an especially great job expressing exasperation as Bass faces plenty of absurd foes, like an outlaw in a rampaging bull mech that requires complex cooperation to take down.

It also brings the Motion Blur tool from iPhone to Android, along with full multi-wheel Color Grading. As a longtime Snapseed fan, I was stoked when Google finally started showing the app some love this year. Since then, the company has rolled out several new features and improved the app in multiple ways. Well, it doesn’t seem like Google is planning to stop anytime soon. Google has started rolling out Snapseed v4.2 on Android and iOS, and the update introduces several new features to the much-loved photo-editing app (via Droid Life ).

articles.excerpt: Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight p…
articles.body: 6 Min Read Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now View of the Manned Spacecraft Center during construction in 1963. Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping to usher in a Golden Age of innovation and discovery. Johnson is home to America’s astronaut corps, the Mission Control Center, and the teams behind some of humanity’s greatest achievements in space.

articles.title: New 'Star Trek: The Original Voyages' book traces the stellar legacy of the bold sci-fi brand
articles.excerpt: Keep the 60th anniversary party going with this visual salute to the series that launched a legacy
articles.body: "Star Trek" celebrated its diamond anniversary last month, marking 60 years since it first aired on NBC on Sept. 8, 1966. There were a bunch of Trekkie-themed celebrations and news stories over September, including festive documentaries , special screenings , tributes, parade floats , interviews, and even a Galileo shuttle story. Now, publishers Penguin Random House and Ten Speed Press are releasing " Star Trek: The Original Voyages: A Visual History " on Nov. 10, 2026. This coffee table book promises unprecedented exploration of the pioneering space fantasy television series and enduring pop culture property that bolstered the space race and ignited sci-fi audiences' imaginations by taking us to strange new worlds and civilizations in the final frontier.
